data.content_ref: inline:The target's mechanism explicitly grounds the Popperian preference in structural features of corroboration: severity of testing, testability, and informativeness for further criticism. This structural grounding is load-bearing — it is what distinguishes the Popperian 'critical rational choice' from mere inductive habit. Yet the mechanism's final sentence — 'It follows that the underlying structure was never relevant to the outcome at all' — directly negates this grounding. If structure is irrelevant, then the severity, testability, and informativeness of corroboration cannot justify the preference, and the central distinction between 'inductive support' and 'corroboration as a report of past performance' (itself a structural distinction) becomes vacuous. The sentence undercuts every prior claim in the same paragraph. No coherent reading rescues it: if 'underlying structure' means the structure of reality, then falsification itself (which requires the world to push back against theories) becomes meaningless, destroying the 'logical asymmetry of falsification' that the claim says grounds the leap of faith. If 'underlying structure' means the shared analogical structure between natural selection and Popperian choice, then the entire analogy section and its transfer claims are rendered superfluous. Either way, the target's own mechanism contains a performative contradiction that invalidates its core defense.
